[element-string-name]
=== `<string-name>` Name of Person (Unstructured)

Container element for personal names captured with mixed-content (both text and elements) where the order of the name components is not enforced and punctuation is preserved.

#### Usage/Remarks
The STS model for <<element-name,`<name>`>> is a series of elements in a particular order with no punctuation or spacing between elements. For situations where a different element order is desired or punctuation between name parts is wanted, use the <<element-string-name,`<string-name>`>>, which is a very loose element, which may contain text, numbers, special characters, generated text, and any or all of the naming elements, such as <<element-surname,`<surname>`>>.
If the name parts are unknown or untagged, put the whole name within the <<element-string-name,`<string-name>`>> element, for example, “`<string-name>Ice Cube</string-name>`”. Use of the <<element-string-name,`<string-name>`>> element is more likely to lead to better searching in a repository than merely leaving the person’s name untagged.

#### Attributes

* <<attribute-content-type,`@content-type`>>
* <<attribute-name-style,`@name-style`>> (default = western)
* <<attribute-specific-use,`@specific-use`>>
#### Base Attributes

* <<attribute-id,`@id`>>
* <<attribute-xml-base,`@xml:base`>>
* <<attribute-xml-lang,`@xml:lang`>>

#### Models and Context

#### May be contained in

<<element-contrib,`<contrib>`>>, <<element-element-citation,`<element-citation>`>>, <<element-mixed-citation,`<mixed-citation>`>>, <<element-name-alternatives,`<name-alternatives>`>>, <<element-person-group,`<person-group>`>>, <<element-related-article,`<related-article>`>>, <<element-related-object,`<related-object>`>>
#### Description

Any combination of: Text, numbers, or special characters <<element-degrees,`<degrees>`>> <<element-degrees,Degree(s)>> <<element-given-names,`<given-names>`>> <<element-given-names,Given (First) Names>> <<element-prefix,`<prefix>`>> <<element-prefix,Prefix (in a name)>> <<element-surname,`<surname>`>> <<element-surname,Surname>> <<element-suffix,`<suffix>`>> <<element-suffix,Suffix (in a name)>>
#### Content Model

[source,xml]
....
<!ELEMENT  string-name  (#PCDATA %string-name-elements;)*            >
....
#### Expanded Content Model

(#PCDATA | degrees | given-names | prefix | surname | suffix)*

#### Tagged Samples

#### As part of bibliographic reference for journal

[source,xml]
....
...
<ref-list>
 <title>Bibliography</title>
 ...
 <ref id="ref_4">
  <label>4</label>
  <mixed-citation publication-type="journal"
   ><person-group
    ><string-name><surname>Hadorn</surname>,  
     <given-names>H.</given-names></string-name>, 
    <string-name><surname>Z&uuml;rchner</surname>,  
     <given-names>K</given-names></string-name></person-group>. 
   <source>Dtsch. Lebensmitt. Rundsch</source>. 
   <year iso-8601-date="1974">1974</year>, 
   <volume>70</volume> p. <fpage>57</fpage></mixed-citation>
 </ref>
 ...
</ref-list>
...
....
